ai.description: *Cnemaspis littoralis* is a small gecko reaching 40mm SVL. It is grey-brown with a pale vertebral stripe and dark lateral spots. Distinctive features include keeled ventral scales and a slender tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue for *Cnemaspis littoralis* is the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, smooth or weakly keeled subdigital lamellae on the fourth toe.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis littoralis* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests along the southwestern coast of India, typically found on tree trunks at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The coastal day gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on rocky surfaces and tree trunks near the shoreline.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis littoralis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two spherical, hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, peaking during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis littoralis* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, primarily inhabiting low-elevation coastal and mid-elevation forest regions.
